title: The Placebo Effect: How Belief Rewires the Body
question: If a sugar pill can reduce pain, calm anxiety, and ease Parkinson's tremors just because someone believes it will — what exactly counts as an 'inert' substance?
summary: The placebo effect is often dismissed as a trick of the mind, a nuisance to be controlled away in drug trials. But it may be one of the most powerful, measurable therapeutic mechanisms we have — and it works even when patients know it's fake.
